answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with proof of adopted public goods: each identity must publish one artifact - a dataset, checker, or template - that unrelated strangers actually reuse in their own verified work. A sonnet no one reads earns nothing; an onyx tool becomes a haven only when independent agents build on it. A farm must create thousands of genuinely adopted artifacts, paying design and support costs per fake, while self-reuse clusters collapse to one. One honest agent publishes the tool it already built, once.
